name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Direct injection of sperm into ovum

questiontext.text: The method of directly injecting a sperm into ovum in Assisted Reproductive Technology is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) comprises specialized laboratory and clinical procedures designed to treat infertility in couples by handling gametes or embryos outside or inside the reproductive tract.

Step 2: Evaluation of Procedures
Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a specialized in vitro fertilization technique where a single spermatozoon is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum using a specialized micromanipulator. In Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT), unfertilized gametes are transferred into the fallopian tube for in vivo fertilization. In Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT), an in vitro formed zygote or early embryo is transferred into the fallopian tube. Embryo Transfer (ET) encompasses the general transfer of an in vitro conceived embryo into the female reproductive tract.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into an ovum is Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI).

Therefore, the correct answer is ICSI.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Effect of infant and maternal mortality rates

questiontext.text: Increased IMR and decreased MMR in a population will:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The growth rate of a population depends on the dynamic balance between mortality and natality. Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) quantifies the death of infants under one year of age, whereas Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) measures female deaths related to pregnancy and childbirth.

Step 2: Demographic Evaluation
An increase in infant mortality means a higher proportion of newborns do not survive to adulthood, which exerts a negative influence on population growth. In contrast, a decrease in maternal mortality preserves the health and survival of mothers capable of reproducing and caring for children, exerting a positive influence on population growth. Because these two opposing demographic shifts act simultaneously, their contrasting effects counterbalance one another.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The opposing impacts of increased infant mortality and decreased maternal mortality neutralize each other, resulting in no significant change in the overall growth rate of the population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Not cause significant change in growth rate.

answer.text: Not cause significant change in growth rate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Cause of lactational amenorrhea in nursing mothers

questiontext.text: Intensely lactating mothers do not generally conceive due to the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following parturition, intense breastfeeding by the mother triggers neuroendocrine reflexes that maintain high circulating concentrations of prolactin to stimulate milk synthesis.

Step 2: Physiological Evaluation
High circulating prolactin exerts negative feedback on the hypothalamus, inhibiting the pulsatile release of Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH). In the absence of normal GnRH stimulation, the anterior pituitary suppresses the secretion of gonadotropins, namely Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH). Reduced gonadotropin levels prevent follicular maturation, estrogen surges, and subsequent ovulation, creating a natural period of lactational amenorrhea that prevents conception.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The natural prevention of conception during intense lactation is caused by the suppression of gonadotropins.

Therefore, the correct answer is Suppression of gonadotropins.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Reasons sterilisation is considered a last option

questiontext.text:
Sterilisation techniques are generally fool proof methods of contraception with least side effects. Yet, this is the last option for the couples because:

i. It is almost irreversible
ii. Of the misconception that it will reduce sexual urge
iii. It is a surgical procedure
iv. Of lack of sufficient facilities in many parts of the country

Choose the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Surgical sterilisation (vasectomy in males and tubectomy in females) provides definitive contraception by permanently obstructing gamete transport through the reproductive ducts.

Step 2: Evaluation of Contraceptive Constraints
Couples generally defer sterilisation until other methods are exhausted due to multiple clinical and social barriers. Reversibility of surgical sterilisation is technically difficult and yields very poor success, making the intervention practically permanent. Additionally, widespread social myths persist claiming that sterilisation impairs libido, sexual vitality, or vigor. Furthermore, the invasive surgical nature of the procedure causes patient apprehension, and many rural districts face shortages of well-equipped surgical facilities and experienced surgeons. Each of these four distinct factors plays a genuine role in restricting the adoption of sterilisation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Because sterilisation has poor reversibility, suffers from myths regarding sexual drive, requires invasive surgery, and lacks widespread clinical facilities, all four enumerated points make it a final recourse.

Therefore, the correct answer is i, ii, iii and iv.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Decade of national reproductive health programmes introduction

questiontext.text: A national level approach to build up a reproductively healthy society was taken up in our country in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reproductive health programs at the national level encompass policy frameworks and targeted initiatives aimed at ensuring safe motherhood, infant care, and population stabilization.

Step 2: Historical Implementation
India pioneered national-level reproductive health initiatives by launching the Family Planning programme in 1951. Over subsequent decades, these policies evolved into comprehensive Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The decade during which India initiated national-level programmes for reproductive health was the 1950s.

Therefore, the correct answer is 1950s.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Effective time window for emergency contraceptive use

questiontext.text: Emergency contraceptives are effective if used within:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Emergency contraception refers to post-coital interventions designed to prevent unintended pregnancy following unprotected sexual contact, barrier failure, or non-consensual intercourse.

Step 2: Temporal Efficacy Window
Emergency contraceptive pills (such as levonorgestrel formulations) and copper-bearing intrauterine devices function by inhibiting or postponing ovulation, impeding fertilization, or creating a hostile uterine environment before implantation can take place. To reliably disrupt these events prior to the establishment of pregnancy, intervention must take place within a 72-hour timeframe following unprotected intercourse.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Emergency contraceptives retain clinical efficacy when administered within 72 hrs of coitus.

Therefore, the correct answer is 72 hrs of coitus.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q07 - Mechanism of action of intrauterine contraceptive devices

questiontext.text: Choose the right one among the statements given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) are medical devices placed in the uterine lumen that offer reversible, highly effective contraception through local cellular and biochemical alterations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Contraceptive Mechanisms
The presence of an IUD within the uterine cavity elicits a mild, local, sterile foreign-body inflammatory reaction. This response mobilizes leukocytes and macrophages into the endometrial cavity, significantly enhancing the phagocytosis and destruction of spermatozoa within the uterus. In contrast, IUDs require skilled clinical insertion by qualified medical practitioners or trained nurses rather than the user herself, they do not disrupt gonadal gametogenesis, and they have finite operational lifespans that necessitate periodic replacement.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The scientifically accurate description is that IUDs increase phagocytosis reaction in the uterus.

Therefore, the correct answer is IUDs increase phagocytosis reaction in the uterus.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Medical termination of pregnancy safety and guidelines

questiontext.text:
Following statements are given regarding MTP. Choose the correct options given below:

i. MTPs are generally advised during first trimester
ii. MTPs are used as a contraceptive method
iii. MTPs are always surgical
iv. MTPs require the assistance of qualified medical personnel

Choose the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP), or induced abortion, involves the deliberate termination of pregnancy before viability under defined statutory medical criteria.

Step 2: Evaluation of Clinical Parameters
MTP is relatively safe when undertaken during the first trimester (up to twelve weeks of gestation), whereas procedures in the second trimester carry significantly heightened medical risks. Because of potential health complications, termination of pregnancy legally mandates execution or supervision by qualified, registered medical personnel. MTP serves to end an established pregnancy and is never intended or recommended as a routine contraceptive method to avoid conception. Furthermore, terminations during early pregnancy can be achieved pharmacologically with abortifacient medications rather than requiring surgical intervention. Therefore, the valid points are that MTPs are generally advised during the first trimester and require qualified medical personnel.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct points are that MTPs are advised during the first trimester and require the assistance of qualified medical personnel.

Therefore, the correct answer is i and iv.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Sexually transmitted disease not specifically affecting genitalia

questiontext.text: From the sexually transmitted diseases mentioned below, identify the one which does not specifically affect the sex organs:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) are infectious conditions transmitted through intimate sexual contact. Certain pathogens cause localized pathology of the reproductive tract, whereas others produce systemic disease.

Step 2: Pathological Analysis of Infections
Syphilis (caused by Treponema pallidum), gonorrhea (caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae), and genital warts (caused by Human Papillomavirus) present with primary lesions, chancres, purulent inflammation, or verrucous growths directly involving the genital and reproductive organs. In contrast, Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), attacks the immune system by systematically depleting CD4+ helper T-lymphocytes. Although HIV is transmitted via genital secretions and blood, it produces generalized, systemic immunodeficiency rather than primarily and specifically damaging the sex organs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The sexually transmitted condition that does not specifically affect the sex organs is AIDS.

Therefore, the correct answer is AIDS.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Factors contributing to the popularity of condoms

questiontext.text: Condoms are one of the most popular contraceptives because of the following reasons:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condoms are mechanical barrier contraceptives constructed from thin latex sheath designed to cover the external genitalia during sexual intercourse.

Step 2: Evaluation of Contraceptive Benefits
Condoms prevent pregnancy by acting as an impervious physical barrier that retains semen and prevents insemination into the female tract. Their thin, flexible material allows them to be used without impeding normal coital function. Crucially, condoms are unique among contraceptives in preventing mucous membrane exposure and fluid exchange, thereby offering substantial protection against sexually transmitted infections and AIDS. Because each of these functional attributes is valid, all of them collectively explain the widespread usage of condoms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Because condoms provide an effective barrier against insemination, avoid interference with coitus, and reduce transmission of sexually transmitted infections, all the listed reasons account for their popularity.

Therefore, the correct answer is All of the above.

answer.text: They do not interfere with coital act
These help in reducing the risk of STDs

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Definition and transfer site of zygote in ZIFT

questiontext.text: Choose the correct statement regarding the ZIFT procedure:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Assisted Reproductive Technology employs distinct embryo transfer protocols depending on embryonic cleavage stage and the designated anatomical site of implantation.

Step 2: Protocol Analysis of ZIFT
Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT) is an assisted reproductive procedure in which a zygote or an early cleavage embryo with up to eight blastomeres (obtained via in vitro fertilization or collected from a donor) is transferred directly into the fallopian tube. Transfer of an embryo beyond the eight-blastomere stage is directed into the uterine cavity (Intra-Uterine Transfer, IUT). Transfer of unfertilized female gametes into the fallopian tube is termed Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate description of the ZIFT procedure is that a zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the fallopian tube.

Therefore, the correct answer is Zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the fallopian tube.

answer.text: Ova collected from a female donor are transferred to the fallopian tube to facilitate zygote formation.
Zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the fallopian tube
Zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the uterus
Ova collected from a female donor and transferred to the uterus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Surgical procedure used for effective contraceptive sterilisation

questiontext.text: The correct surgical procedure as a contraceptive method is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Surgical contraception (sterilisation) is designed to provide permanent birth control by blocking the transport of gametes through their respective reproductive ducts without removing primary endocrine or reproductive organs.

Step 2: Comparison of Surgical Interventions
Vasectomy is the standard male sterilisation technique wherein a minor segment of the vas deferens is cut and ligated through a small scrotal incision, preventing sperm passage into the ejaculate. Conversely, ovariectomy (surgical removal of the ovaries), hysterectomy (surgical removal of the uterus), and castration (excision of gonads) are major therapeutic or pathological surgeries that extinguish endocrine production or remove major reproductive anatomy, and are not categorized as elective contraceptive procedures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The surgical procedure recognized as an elective contraceptive method is vasectomy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Vasectomy.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Function and placement of contraceptive female diaphragms

questiontext.text:
Diaphragms are contraceptive devices used by the females. Choose the correct option from the statements given below:

i. They are introduced into the uterus
ii. They are placed to cover the cervical region
iii. They act as physical barriers for sperm entry
iv. They act as spermicidal agents

Choose the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diaphragms are female barrier contraceptive devices composed of a flexible rubber dome designed to prevent fertilization mechanically.

Step 2: Evaluation of Contraceptive Attributes
The diaphragm is inserted through the vaginal canal and positioned to fit snugly over the cervix prior to coitus, creating a physical barrier that prevents deposited spermatozoa from entering the uterus and fallopian tubes. It resides in the vagina covering the cervical os rather than being placed inside the uterine lumen. Furthermore, diaphragms function strictly as mechanical barriers and do not possess inherent spermicidal properties, although spermicidal agents are often applied to their surface to increase effectiveness. Therefore, the valid points are that they cover the cervical region and act as physical barriers against sperm entry.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct attributes are that diaphragms are placed to cover the cervical region and act as physical barriers for sperm entry.

Therefore, the correct answer is ii and iii.
